plan.chapterName: OpenStax Organic Chemistry, chapter 27: Biomolecules: Lipids
plan.contextChunk: This figure sets a three-dimensional rendering of a lipid bilayer beside the flat structural formula of the molecule that builds it. On the left, a slab of membrane is drawn in perspective with a stepped cutaway at one corner: rows of small green spheres tile the top and bottom faces, and the interior between them is packed with pale tan wavy strands that meet tip to tip along the slab's midplane, so the two leaflets face each other tails inward. On the right, a glycerophospholipid is drawn with a vertical glycerol backbone reading CH2, CH, CH2 from top to bottom. The topmost branch is printed in green and reads CH2-O-P(=O)(O-)-O-CH2CH2N(CH3)3+, tagged by a green arrow labeled "Ionic head". The two lower branches each run through O-C(=O) into a long tan ribbon of the same shade and waviness as the strands filling the slab, and a magenta label "Nonpolar tails" sends two arrows to their free ends. Matching the green and tan across the two halves lets the reader place each region of the drawn molecule at its position in the assembled sheet. The pairing accounts for how a long nonpolar tail bound to a polar ionic head drives aggregation into a bilayer that keeps hydrocarbon away from water.

elements: bilayer slab on the left, roughly 10 × 2.4 × 7 units, with a stepped cutaway corner exposing the interior
top leaflet of green head-group spheres tiling the slab's upper face in a hexagonal-ish lattice
bottom leaflet of green head-group spheres tiling the lower face
two layers of pale tan wavy hydrocarbon strands filling the slab interior, meeting tip-to-tip at the midplane (tails inward)
glycerophospholipid structural formula on the right, drawn as a flat diagram floating beside the slab: vertical glycerol backbone CH2 / CH / CH2
green ionic head branch: CH2-O-P(=O)(O-)-O-CH2CH2N(CH3)3+ extending from the top backbone carbon
two tan wavy nonpolar tail ribbons extending rightward from the lower backbone carbons through O-C(=O) ester links
green annotation arrow labeled 'Ionic head' pointing to the phosphate group
magenta label 'Nonpolar tails' with two arrows pointing to the tail tips

interactions.teaches: Clicking the ionic head, glycerol linker, or nonpolar tails highlights that region in both the structural formula and the bilayer slab simultaneously, mapping one molecule's amphiphilic parts onto their positions in the assembled membrane

interactions.label: View
interactions.teaches: Switching to assembly mapping overlays the head/linker/tail color coding onto the whole membrane slab, showing that the bilayer is nothing but many copies of the drawn molecule arranged heads-out, tails-in

interactions.label: Cutaway depth
interactions.teaches: Sweeping the slice plane through the slab successively exposes the outer head layer, the tail region, and the midplane where the two leaflets' tails meet, revealing the polar-outside / nonpolar-inside organization through the membrane's thickness

demo_steps.title: Intact membrane
demo_steps.narration: The slab shows green head-group spheres on both outer faces with tails hidden inside. This is how the membrane presents itself to water on both sides.

demo_steps.title: Slice into the tails
demo_steps.narration: Drag the cutaway slider midway: the slice peels back a corner to expose the tan hydrocarbon strands packed between the two head layers.

demo_steps.title: Midplane contact
demo_steps.narration: At full cutaway the two leaflets are seen meeting tail-tip to tail-tip at the midplane — the hallmark of a bilayer: polar heads out, nonpolar tails in.

demo_steps.title: Map molecule to membrane
demo_steps.narration: Switch to assembly mapping: the head, linker, and tail colors of the single molecule light up the corresponding regions of the whole slab, connecting the formula to the aggregate.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Overall figure spans ~±9 units in X: bilayer slab centered at (-4.5, 0, 0), sized ~7 wide (X) × 2.4 tall (Y, the membrane normal) × 6 deep (Z); head spheres ~0.28 radius in green #58c98a, spaced ~0.6 apart in a close-packed lattice on the top (y=+1.2) and bottom (y=-1.2) faces; tails are tan #d9a98c wavy tube strands ~1.0 long per leaflet, drooping inward from each head sphere to meet tip-to-tip at the midplane y=0. Stepped cutaway at the front-right corner of the slab as in the source. The structural formula occupies the right half as a flat diagram (x from +1 to +9): vertical glycerol backbone at x≈+1.2 with CH2 (y≈+1.0), CH (y≈0), CH2 (y≈-1.0); ionic head branch in green extends up-right from the top carbon (P with =O, O−, then O-CH2CH2-N+(CH3)3, label 'Ionic head' in green with arrow); two ester links O-C(=O) at y≈0 and y≈-1.0 lead into long tan wavy ribbons running horizontally right to x≈+8, with magenta 'Nonpolar tails' label and arrows to the free tips. Colors must match across halves: head green #58c98a, tails tan #d9a98c, glycerol/linker dark grey text, 'Nonpolar tails' label magenta #c0328a, 'Ionic head' label dark green #1e7a4c.
interactionPlan.notes: Render the formula as flat textured sprites/curves (three.js text sprites for atom labels, TubeGeometry with sine-wave centerlines for the tail ribbons) lying in a plane facing the camera on the right side, so both halves share one perspective scene. Implement cutaway as a clipping plane or progressive sphere/strand culling keyed to the slider: heads vanish first from the sliced corner, then tails, so the midplane tail-to-tail contact is exposed at slider=1. Click targets: three invisible hit regions (head branch, backbone, tail pair) on the formula plus matching hit regions on the slab; selection applies an emissive glow to both copies at once. In Assembly mapping mode, tint all slab heads green-glowing and tails tan-glowing with the glycerol ester region marked between them. Keep poly counts modest: use InstancedMesh for head spheres and a few dozen pre-generated strand geometries reused by instance.

- Click ionic head, glycerol linker, or nonpolar tails: the selected part highlights in the molecule and in the bilayer slab, mapping amphiphilic structure to membrane organization.
- Toggle between molecule and assembly mapping: switch named highlights for ionic head, glycerol linker, and nonpolar tails, and matching regions glow on both the structural formula and membrane slab, showing how each part of one glycerophospholipid maps into the bilayer.

authoredContext:
Phospholipids are found widely in both plant and animal tissues and make up approximately 50% to 60% of cell membranes. Because they are like soaps in having a long, nonpolar hydrocarbon tail bound to a polar ionic head, phospholipids in the cell membrane organize into a lipid bilayer about 5.0 nm (50 Å) thick. As shown in the figure, the nonpolar tails aggregate in the center of the bilayer in much the same way that soap tails aggregate in the center of a micelle. This bilayer serves as an effective barrier to the passage of water, ions, and other components into and out of cells.

Aggregation of glycerophospholipids into the lipid bilayer that composes cell membranes.

Glycerophospholipids combine with the lipid bilayer comprising a cell membrane. An arrow points to the ionic head and two nonpolar tails of the lipid bilayer.

discrepancies: Slab head spheres are a noticeably darker, saturated green than the light mint green of the source
An extra 'Lipid bilayer' label appears that is not in the source figure
In the source, the two magenta 'Nonpolar tails' arrows clearly point to the two separate tails; in the render both arrows cluster at the bottom-right near the tail tips

The 'Ionic head' callout text in the source sits at the top with an arrow to the phosphate; the generated label floats high with its arrow pointing only at the P region, roughly matching but placement differs
Formula atom layout is slightly compressed/shifted relative to the source (P=O double bond and O⁻ positions)
evaluation.notes: Strong reconstruction: bilayer slab with green heads and tan tails plus the structural formula with correct ionic-head/nonpolar-tail annotations; rich interactions (cutaway slider, demo steps, click-to-highlight mapping) enhance teaching value, marred mainly by the too-dark head color and a hallucinated 'Lipid bilayer' label.
action_items: Lighten the head-sphere color toward the source's pale mint green (#8fdcb0 range)
Remove the 'Lipid bilayer' label, which does not appear in the source
Spread the two magenta tail arrows so one points at each of the two tail ribbons as in the source
Tune the formula atom positions so the P=O double bond and O⁻ arrangement above phosphorus matches the source more closely

feedback.rationale: Scores are consistently high (4–5 across all dimensions, overall 4.4) with concept accuracy and interactivity at 5; the remaining issues (darker head color, one hallucinated label, arrow placement) are minor visual polish that do not justify further iteration.
